key_sub: Double the distance → one quarter of the force.
body_html:
How to think about it

Every particle in the universe attracts every other particle with a force that is proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centres: F = Gm₁m₂/r², with G = 6,67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²·kg⁻².

The gravitational field strength at a planet's surface is g = GM/R². Mass is the amount of matter and is the same everywhere; weight is the gravitational force on an object and depends on g.

Example

The distance between two masses is tripled. New force?

Inverse square: 1/3²

Answer: one ninth of the original

Example

A 60 kg astronaut on the Moon (g = 1,6 m·s⁻²). Weight?

w = mg

Answer: 96 N

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to square the distance.
  • Measuring r from the surface instead of the centre.
  • Thinking mass changes on the Moon.

faq.q: Why do astronauts float in the International Space Station?
faq.a: They and the station are falling around the Earth together (free fall); gravity still acts on them.

faq.q: Does the Earth pull on you more than you pull on the Earth?
faq.a: No; by Newton's third law the forces are equal, but the Earth's huge mass means its acceleration is tiny.
